text:
The Red Wings are a week into life after Dylan Larkin, and so far the answer to the question everyone in Detroit has been asking is John Gibson. He stopped all 18 shots in a 2-0 win at Columbus on Friday afternoon, and he did it on a day when the Blue Jackets had clearly the better chances.

Detroit scored first and early enough to settle in. J.T. Compher snapped one home at 11:51 of the first, set up by Ben Chiarot and Moritz Seider, and the Wings led despite losing that period 1.16 to 0.57 in expected goals (the quality of chances, added up). Columbus pushed harder in the second, 1.34 to 0.73, and Luca Del Bel Belluz had the best look of the game, a 34% chance that missed the net. Gibson handled the rest.

Alex DeBrincat doubled the lead at 4:37 of the third on an 8% snap shot from Lucas Raymond and Albert Johansson, a goal that moved Detroit's win chance from 75% to 91%. The biggest save came later, on Adam Fantilli from in close, a 32% chance. Gibson finished about 3.3 goals better than the shots he faced deserved and added 0.62 wins on his own, roughly four times anyone else in the game. Jet Greaves was fine at the other end, 19 saves on 21 shots and right at expected. Detroit also blocked 20 shots to Columbus's nine.

Our replays of every shot gave the Blue Jackets the win 72% of the time, and they outattempted Detroit 62 to 42. Rick Bowness's team will look at this one as a game it should have taken, especially at home. For Todd McLellan's Red Wings, it is a second straight win since the trade that sent Larkin to Montreal, after Wednesday's 5-1 win over Vancouver. You can argue about how much of this is sustainable when the goalie has to be this good. You can't argue that Gibson, at a moment when the franchise needed a calm night, gave it one.
headline: Gibson steals a Black Friday shutout in Columbus
